I'm in a band and we're looking to record a first demo. But being all in (or recently graduated from) high school, we don't have much money. I think the drums will need the most mics, so I'm wondering how to record them using the fewest mics possible. I don't need a professional quality recording, I just want it to sound decent.
How do I record drums with as few mics as possible?

There are a few 2 mic techniques for recording drums.

Check out this article on stereo mic techniques.

http://music.tutsplus.com/tutorials/6-stereo-miking-techniques-you-can-use-today--audio-204

Also look up the Recorderman technique.

Can you provide a list of the equipment you're currently working with, or a projected budget (even if it's <200/300$) if you don't have any equipment? Are the mics you have for band practice AKG vocal mics or Shure sm57's? If so could possible work with one of those for your snare sound. If you could include your A/D converter, how many channels, etc I can help you out. I have my own studio now as of 3 years, but spent almost 10 years doing exactly what you are doing!

Edit: The quick/best answer was already given by Fnordpocalypse - stereo miking - provided you only have channels to work with.

This would be my recommended list of mics for drums, from less to more:

  • one overhead, move it around and find a spot that captures the whole drumkit and gives you a balanced sound.
  • one overhead + kick drum mic. Same as above
  • two overheads + kick drum mic.
  • two overheads, mic kick and snare.
  • two overheads, kick, snare, toms.
  • two overheads, kick, snare, toms, 1-2 room mics.

It helps a lot if your drummer is good at balancing the volume of all the individual parts of the drumkit so one mic can pick up every element decently. Also, move the kit and the mics around in the room and record a little to find the best spot in the room to capture the drums.

Good luck!
